response: Yes, end-tidal carbon dioxide measurement correlates with arterial carbon dioxide in extremely low birth weight infants in the first week of life. There is good correlation and agreement between end-tidal CO(2) and arterial CO(2) in ELBW infants, particularly in the EtCO(2) range of 30-50 mmHg. This suggests that end-tidal CO(2) monitoring can be a helpful tool for trending or screening abnormal PaCO(2) values in ELBW infants during the first week of life.
